forecast.seasonality_note: Scout did not confirm seasonality for the term (search_terms notes); the earlier run assumed a mild January 'organise my life' and September office-setup uptick, and Q4 raises storage cost rather than demand for a desk pad, so no seasonal adjustment is applied beyond the ranges.
forecast.reasoning: Outside in (forecast.reference_class, forecast.fermi): scout has no tracker volumes, so term volume is a Fermi estimate from review velocity, about 5,700 units a month on 'elbow pad for desk' (3,300-8,500) at an assumed 2-5% review-per-order rate, and that rate is the assumption to audit first. Our share: the buyer clicks VAYDEER or JIKIOU 65% of the time today (gate.social_proof) and competition gives us 0.12 as the chosen tile at launch, falling to 0.07 once twins arrive; a zero-review tile at $23.99 starts on page two, months 1-3 are innovator-only (rogers.innovators, moore.chasm), Vine plus the card's review trigger bring 50-80 reviews by month 6 and 100-150 by month 12, which keeps us inside the chasm against 791 and 2,045 but past the 30-review floor, so 2.5% of the term by month 6 (35-425 sets, base 140) and 4% by month 12 (50-680, base 230), year one 380-4,900, base 1,650 sets. These share numbers are the PRE-clone window: competition rates copycat risk high, twins in 1-6 months at $12.99-16.99 and a 35% haircut, and the engine applies that haircut itself (monte_carlo_cloned), so the cloned base is about 150 sets in month 12 and 1,070 in the year; the wave is deliberately not baked into the shares to avoid a double haircut. Set versus single: the pair is the row's form (nine of twelve tiles, F9) and halves the fulfilment fee per pad ($5.30 for two against $4.76 for one, both large standard because the moulded L is 65 mm tall); the single at $17.99 earns about $0.80 more contribution per pad at base because the buyer pays $17.99 for one pad (VAYDEER, F11) against about $12 a pad in the set, but it sells one pad an order, fights the 2,045-review leader at its own price (competition threat high) and the buyer has a two-forearm problem (N6), so the pair is recommended. Neither version clears the 15% post-advertising floor at today's landed cost (set at $23.99 roughly -2 a set at base, single at $17.99 roughly break-even, v1_lean at $23.99 roughly break-even), which is why the fix is the tariff tranche and the EXW, not the pack count.

phases.phase: DFM and quotes: profile CAD for the one-piece L, two factory quotes on the full spec at MOQ 300 and 1,000, written confirmation that $5.75 is per set (F25), broker opinion on the HTS line and the 301 tranche (F20-F22)

weeks.assumption: 2-4 calendar weeks before the multiplier (base 3), times 1.35; the broker opinion and the second quote run in parallel with the CAD.

phases.phase: Prototypes and fit tests: the new profile die, two sample rounds air-freighted, seating on a 25 mm square edge and a 38 mm R5 eased edge, the edge-load bottoming test (I1), and weighing and cubing the nested box against the live FBA rate card

weeks.assumption: 3-5 weeks before the multiplier (base 4), times 1.35; a foam die turns in days, the air freight and the second round set the floor.

phases.phase: Lab gates: the 500 h humidity-aged peel (three weeks on its own), compression set, 80,000-cycle fatigue, COF on five surfaces, 20 washes, zip cycles, chamber sniff (I2-I4, I6); photography, listing copy, the design filing and Brand Registry run in parallel

weeks.assumption: 3-5 weeks before the multiplier (base 4), times 1.35; the humidity ageing is the critical path and cannot be shortened, and a failed peel gate adds a full round.

phases.phase: Production: die sign-off, first run of 300-1,000 sets with the 7-day open-rack foam rest (I6), pre-shipment inspection, packing in the taller kraft mailer with the card and no bag

weeks.assumption: 4-6 weeks before the multiplier (base 5), times 1.35; includes the seven rest days and a factory queue behind larger orders.

phases.phase: Sea freight LCL China to US West Coast, customs entry under the broker's classification, FBA check-in and the first organic order

weeks.assumption: 5-7 weeks before the multiplier (base 6), times 1.35; port-to-port 30-45 days on scout's stale freight assumption plus one to two weeks of receiving.

weeks_to_first_sale.assumption: The five phases summed: 17-27 weeks before the multiplier (base 22, inside the knowledge base's 20-34 because the tooling is a foam die, not a steel injection tool), times the 1.35 planning-fallacy multiplier stated above (forecast.planning_fallacy); the high of 37 already carries one extra sample round and clears the 39-week rail by two weeks, so a second die re-cut or a failed humidity-aged peel would break that rail.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the memory shell lifted and bunched at the R20 roll on pads that spent a summer in a 30 C room, and three matching one-stars on 'the top layer came loose' sank the rating to 4.1: the category's adhesive obituary, transposed to the one bond we kept (C2, N5).
premortem.mitigation: The humidity-aged peel gate (at least 1 N/cm after 500 h at 40 C / 80% RH, ASTM D903) on the T1 sample and on every production lot, the memory shell cut as its own L so the bond is never in peel at the roll, and the vulcanised-through base with no glue line (I2, I3, innovaty durability_review).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Peel tests on two lots plus a retained-sample programme; already partly inside the lab-test NRE line.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and three 2-packs with a rounded no-fold corner appeared on page one between months 2 and 5 at $12.99-14.99, re-cut from an open foam die, took the price-sensitive two-thirds of our clicks, and we sold 35% fewer sets than planned. This agrees with competition's read: copycat risk high, first clone in 1-6 months, clone price $12.99-16.99, haircut 35% (competition.copycat_risk, price_war).
premortem.mitigation: The design application and Brand Registry on file before launch so exact copies of the registered profile are reportable (competition moat design_registration, medium); the spec edge made visible in image 3 (sectioned pad, ruler, bare base on glass) so a clone's thin single-density pad reads as the pad the buyer was burned by (gate.image_2_to_6, law.shape_memory); the Alibaba 'elbow pad desk' page watched weekly as the 6-10-week leading indicator (competition.watch_signals); a 50-reviews-a-month velocity target against JIKIOU's; and no price match below $19.99, because the margin cannot fund one.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Design filing plus trademark (already in the NRE) plus an hour a week of takedown and watch time; the haircut itself is simulated by the engine, not mitigated here.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the nested box for two moulded Ls cubed at 1.3 lb dimensional weight instead of 1.2, Amazon re-tiered the set, and the fulfilment fee came in $0.35-0.90 a set above plan on every unit: the packaging-over-the-line obituary, because the moulded L no longer packs flat and the box grew about 1 cm (innovaty packaging note).
premortem.mitigation: Fix the nested box at or under 30.5 x 12 x 7.2 cm (about 165 in3) and the set at or under 500 g, weigh and cube the T1 sample against the live rate card before the die is signed off (timeline phase 2), cap pad weight at 200 g with the 45/60 kg/m3 build rather than the sample's 250 g, and never let the card or a sleeve add a layer.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: One dieline iteration and a cubing check; the fee difference is already inside the fba_fee_usd range.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the China stack on our line moved from the 17.5-30% we planned to 45-56% between the deposit and the entry, adding $1.00-1.70 a set, and the first 1,000 sets landed at a loss before advertising: the origin-tariff obituary, on a stack that went from 2.3% to 33.9% effective in one year (F22).
premortem.mitigation: A broker's written classification and tranche on 8473.30.5100 versus 9404.90 before the first entry (F20, F21); the first order capped at 1,000 sets; a Vietnam or Indonesia foam-and-sewing second source sampled at the prototype stage so the second order can change origin; the price held at $23.99-24.99 rather than $19.99 so there is room to absorb one step.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Broker opinion $150-400 plus one Vietnam sample round and its air freight $200-1,400.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the 'plastic-free packaging' bullet was flagged under Amazon's environmental-claims policy and the listing sat suppressed for nine days in month 3 while the clones ranked: the suppressed-claim obituary (innovaty sustainability claims).
premortem.mitigation: Word the box line as 'ships in a paper box with no plastic bag' and the cover line as 'OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certified knit, certificate on file', never 'eco', 'green' or 'plastic-free product'; keep the certificate number on the tag and in Seller Central; keep 'replaceable cover' as the longevity claim, which is the strongest one (innovation playbook 7).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: A copy review; nothing physical changes.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and we reached 38 reviews by month 6 and 90 by month 12 against VAYDEER's 2,045 and JIKIOU's 791, the tile never left page two on 'elbow pad for desk', ads bought every order at 45% and the forecast's month-12 volume never arrived: the review-velocity obituary (moore.chasm, gate.social_proof, competition watch_signals).
premortem.mitigation: Vine on 30 sets at launch; the card's review trigger with a QR beside the spec and the two-year promise (post.review_trigger, I5); Amazon's review-request button on every order; a $19.99 launch price for the first 60 days against the $23.99 list; and a hard check at month 4: under 30 reviews means the ad budget stops and the price war is not fought, so the loss is bounded.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Vine fee plus 30 sets at landed cost (in the NRE) plus a $4 launch discount on the first 300 sets.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the quoted supplier re-priced innovaty's spec at $7.80 a set, the tariff stack stayed near 30%, the set landed at $11 against a $23.99 price, and every unit lost money after the 15% referral, the $5.30 fulfilment fee and the launch advertising: the plan was signed on a $5.75 quote for a different, simpler pad (F25) and the 30-40% margin was never there.
premortem.mitigation: No deposit until two numbers are in writing: a broker's tariff tranche at or under 17.5% on the confirmed HTS line, and an EXW at or under $5.00 a set at MOQ 1,000 for the full spec from one of two factories; if either fails, ship v1_lean (I1, I3, I5, I6: one 60 kg/m3 core, a sewn wipe-clean knit, no zip) at $24.99, about $2.10 a set cheaper landed, and treat I2 and I4 as the v1.1 upgrade funded from the first margin; if both fail, the product does not ship as a 2-pack from China at this price and the founder re-briefs on origin or price.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: A second factory's sample rounds and air freight; the broker opinion is in the tariff item above.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the coil zip on the lip jammed on the knit edge or its tape stitching let go on the first wash for about one buyer in twenty, and the washable-cover delighter became the one-star pattern (I4, N3, gate.reviews_negative_first).
premortem.mitigation: A named SBS or YKK #3 coil, the slider garage and bar-tacked ends innovaty specified, 500 open-close cycles and 20 washes on the T1 sample before sign-off, the cord puller instead of metal, and the care step shown on the card (cold wash, air dry).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Branded zips add about $0.03-0.08 a pad on the first order plus the cycle test in the lab line.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the $5.75 turned out to be per piece in the set configuration, not per set, the ambiguity scout flagged in F25; the real set EXW was $11.50 and nothing in the $15-25 band could carry it.
premortem.mitigation: A written pro-forma invoice stating EXW per 2-piece set, incoterm, MOQ, box and carton spec before any deposit, cross-checked against the two Alibaba 1-piece prices (F23, F24) which cap a bare pad at about $3.20.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: An email and a pro-forma; an hour of the founder's time.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and 'does not fit my desk' was the top return reason: aprons, keyboard trays, bullnose edges and tops over 38 mm sent 9% of sets back and the stars fell with them (fear 2, N2, C3, post.return_reason).
premortem.mitigation: The honest fit limit (18-38 mm, square or eased up to R5, 50 mm of clear desk face, not bullnose) in the first bullet, on the card and as a dimensioned drawing in image 2 (innovaty honest_limitations, cialdini.reciprocity), a 'measure your edge' line in the back half of the title, and the R6 relief that seats eased edges flat (I1).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: The dimensioned drawing and the card artwork, inside the listing-graphics NRE line.

idea_rulings.why: A one-piece L on a foam die in the $200-1,100 class, not a steel tool (the supplier's mould is $230, F25), and the only change a stranger sees at 300 px; its cost is that the set no longer packs flat, which keeps it large standard, where the 590 g sample already was.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: +$0.20-0.40 a pad for 945 cm3 of foam against the sample's 600 cm3, on a $200-1,100 die

idea_rulings.why: Two densities with a PUR web are the right answer to N1 and N5 and cost about $0.45 a pad over one 60 kg/m3 core on a set that already fails the contribution floor; it stays in v1 only if the full-spec EXW at MOQ 1,000 comes in at or under $5.00 a set, else it is the v1.1 upgrade.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: +$0.90 a set (base) for the second layer and the web, against a $5.00 EXW ceiling

idea_rulings.why: A vulcanised scrim panel on both faces is $0.24 a pad against $0.05-0.10 of dots or strips, removes the C3 one-star and the adhesive baggie (F7), and is the base the buyer asked to see bare on glass.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: +$0.15 a pad net over dots or strips

idea_rulings.why: A zip with garage and bar-tacks plus its sewing is about $0.35 a pad for a delighter the buyer would also accept as a shown wipe-clean step (buyer.comfort_and_laziness); funded only inside the $5.00 EXW ceiling, else v1.1 with the replacement-cover SKU.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: +$0.35 a pad including labour, +$0.70 a set

idea_rulings.why: A woven tag is $0.03-0.06 a pad and the two-year promise costs about $0.07 a set at a 2% claim rate on a $3-4 replacement cover; it is the physical carrier of the spec edge competition rated medium and costs cents.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: $0.10 a set all-in, tag plus the promise's expected claim cost

idea_rulings.why: A 7-day rack rest, a PUR web and no poly bag net $0.05-0.10 a set (the web costs about what the bag saved) and add seven days to the first run; it answers C2 at 30% of negatives and is the cheapest fix in the plan.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: 7 days on the first run and under $0.10 a set

idea_rulings.why: Four plated N35 discs in sewn pockets are $0.25-0.40 a set plus an FTO read on magnet-joined cushions (medium prior art); innovaty's own unlock needs contribution at or above 30% at launch and the base case as costed is negative, so it stays in v2 and is not in any funded version.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: unlock at 30% contribution against a negative base contribution; +$0.25-0.40 a set

regulatory: Prop 65 (California): polyurethane foam can carry listed flame retardants such as TDCPP; require the supplier's written declaration of no listed FR on the foam lot or carry the warning on the box; no CPSC or children's-product testing applies to an adult desk accessory with no magnets in v1.

FTC Textile Fiber Products Identification Act and country of origin: '100% polyester cover' and 'Made in China' on the woven tag and the box; the OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certificate number kept on file for the claim; no 'eco' or 'biodegradable' wording on PU foam (innovaty rejected_claims).

No FCC, UL or CE applies to a passive foam pad; the two-year flatten-or-peel promise is a seller warranty and must be honoured as written under Amazon's claims policy; if I7 ships in v2 the listing states the magnets are sewn captive and the product is not for children.
three_sentences_to_founder: Your 30-40% is a pre-advertising margin, and at the pair's $5.30 large-standard fulfilment fee plus the 15% referral it needs the landed set at or under roughly $4.70 at $19.99, $6.20 at $22.99 and $7.30 at $24.99 for 30%, and roughly $2.80, $4.00 and $4.80 for 40% (the engine prints the exact figures); the $5.75 quote itself lands at about $8.30-9.90 after the stale 17.5-45% China tariff and freight, above every one of those ceilings.

A cheaper factory for innovaty's spec does not exist: the bottom-up EXW is $6.41 a set at MOQ 300 (realistic negotiated $6.50-8.00, or $5.50-6.80 at MOQ 1,000), above the $5.75 quote, because the two-layer core, the zipped washable cover and the vulcanised base on both faces add about $1.00-1.40 a pad to the folded single-density sample the quote was for, and the $3.09-3.20 Alibaba pads are the thin, bare pads the buyer is trying not to buy.

Ship the pair, not a single (a single moulded L still costs $4.76 to fulfil because it is 65 mm tall and cannot be small standard, and it fights VAYDEER's 2,045 reviews at the same $17.99), but sign nothing until a broker confirms the tariff tranche at or under 17.5% and a factory confirms $5.00 a set or less at MOQ 1,000 in writing: as costed today the contribution after advertising is negative at every price in the band, with both fixes it is only about 7% at $24.99 against the engine's 15% floor (about 28% before advertising, which is your target), so the plan is unrealistic as costed and FIX-FIRST, not dead.
